history.summary: Large freehold 3BR asking $1,354 psf - at the very bottom of the project's range - but extreme thin-cohort data (1 comp), tiny 30-unit illiquid boutique, and maintenance complaints make the 'cheap' tag a likely data quirk.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,354 psf is at the absolute floor of the project's PSF band ($1,354-1,714) and well below the Sep-2025 high ($1,460,000), so on paper it looks like a bargain large 1,238sf 3BR. But the signals are fragile: psf_cohort_txns=1 and appreciation_txns=7, so the eye-catching -29% age-adj premium and -7.2% cohort discount rest on a single comparable - exactly the data quirk v3.4 priors warn against. The development is a 30-unit boutique with only ~13 lifetime sales (very poor exit liquidity), trailing appreciation is negative (-0.49%), and reviews flag MCST maintenance/safety concerns. Freehold is not a forward edge and D14 (RCR) lags OCR on realized forward returns. The large quantum (~$1.68m) in Geylang narrows the buyer pool further. Cheap-looking but not a defensible bargain.
red_flags: psf_cohort_txns=1 and appreciation_txns=7 - both extremely thin; the -29% cheapness is a likely data artifact, not a real discount
Only ~13 lifetime sales in a 30-unit boutique - very poor resale liquidity
Reviews cite MCST maintenance and safety concerns
Large ~$1.68m quantum for a 3BR in Geylang narrows the buyer pool
catalysts: Walking distance to two MRT stations and Geylang amenities
Freehold tenure with no lease decay
Large 1,238sf 3BR layout rare in the price band if owner-occupier demand emerges

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Negative trailing CAGR on just 7 txns - no forward signal. No identifiable dated catalyst. Treat as flat-to-negative.
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Project rentals reported ~$1,900-3,000 (small-unit skew); a 3BR would command more but yield is unremarkable and the boutique scale limits rental comps. Not a yield play.
